newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain heralds election of European Parliament head.
newsitem.headline: Spain heralds election of European Parliament head.

text.p: Spain said it was delighted with the appointment on Tuesday of Partido Popular member Jose-Maria Gil-Robles as head of the European Parliament, saying it reflected Spain's growing role on the international stage.
"We're thrilled about this," Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told a local news agency.

Gil-Robles was elected as president of the European Union's Strasbourg-based parliament by 344 votes to 177 against the only other contender, Catherine Lalumiere of France. He will hold the office until the next parliamentary elections in June 1999.
Matutues said Gil-Robles was a "committed European" who fiercely defended the cornerstones of dialogue and accord.
"He will run the institution with ability and tact at an important time," Matutes said.
Gil-Robles' appointment adds to Spain's already high profile in the international arena.

In December alone, former Spanish Prime Minister Felipe Gonzalez agreed to head a European mission to Yugoslavia and NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, a former foreign minister, was authorised to open talks with Russia on a historic charter with the alliance.
